text.p: Following are the main stories n Estonian newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The average pension will increase to over 1,000 kroons after January 1.
- New traffic insurance regulations will come into force in January 1997, obliging insurers to sign short-term agreements on motor-car insurance.
- Police have found a two-year-old boy who was kidnapped in Tallinn on Christmas Day.
- The representative of Chechnya in Estonia, Imran Akhayev, denies that Jaanus Raidal is to replace him.

- Chairman of the Agrarian party, Arnold Ruutel, said 1996 has been more successful for the Estonian farmer than 1995. But he said the customs control of food imports was still a major problem to be solved.
- According to statistics, the Estonian population has fallen by 100,000 people during 1996.
